content.page_title: Guideline recommendations (heart failure comorbidities and special situations)
content.summary: Recommendations for management of patients with heart failure (HF) and common comorbidities or conditions.

points: Aortic valve intervention (TAVI or SAVR) is recommended in patients with HF and severe high-gradient aortic stenosis to reduce mortality and improve symptoms.
Choice between TAVI and SAVR should be made by the Heart Team considering age, surgical risk, clinical, anatomical and procedural aspects.

SGLT2 inhibitors (examples listed: canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of cardiovascular events to reduce hospitalizations for HF, major CV events, end-stage renal dysfunction and CV death.
SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM and HFrEF to reduce hospitalizations for HF and CV death.
Thiazolidinediones (glitazones) are not recommended in patients with HF (increase risk of HF worsening and hospitalization).
The DPP-4 inhibitor saxagliptin is not recommended in patients with HF.
All patients with HF should be periodically screened for anaemia and iron deficiency with CBC, serum ferritin and TSAT.
Treatment of anaemia in HF with erythropoiesis-stimulating agents is not recommended in the absence of other indications for this therapy.
Adaptive servo-ventilation is not recommended in patients with HFrEF and predominant central sleep apnoea (increased all-cause and CV mortality).
NSAIDs or COX-2 inhibitors are not recommended in patients with HF (increase risk of HF worsening and hospitalization).
Cancer patients at increased risk for cardiotoxicity should undergo CV evaluation before scheduled anticancer therapy, preferably by cardiologist experienced in cardio-oncology.

Tafamidis is recommended in patients with genetically proven hereditary transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (hATTR-CA) and NYHA class I or II symptoms to reduce symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality.
Tafamidis is also recommended in patients with wild-type transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (wtTTR-CA) and NYHA class I or II to reduce symptoms, CV hospitalization and mortality.

genes.context: Guideline recommends tafamidis for patients with genetically proven hATTR-CA and for wtTTR-CA; abbreviations hATTR-CA and wtTTR-CA appear in recommendations and abbreviation list.
BNP and NT-proBNP are listed in the abbreviations as B-type natriuretic peptide and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, markers used in HF management.

Associated Conditions: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; heart failure (treatment target of SGLT2 inhibitors)
genes.context: The page refers to SGLT2 inhibitors (sodium‑glucose co‑transporter 2) recommended for patients with T2DM and HF; SGLT2 corresponds to the SLC5A2 gene product.

Associated Conditions: Hypertension; heart failure (target of ACE inhibitors)
genes.context: ACE-I is defined in the abbreviations (angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor), a primary drug class referenced in HF care on the page.
